questions.question: static/relative/absolute/fixed/sticky — and display:none vs visibility:hidden vs opacity:0: how do the pairs differ?
questions.title: Positioning And Hiding
questions.direct_answer: POSITION: static (normal flow, top/left ignored), relative (flows normally, offsets VISUALLY from its flow position — keeps its gap), absolute (out of flow; positioned vs nearest positioned ancestor; others close the gap), fixed (out of flow; vs viewport — UNLESS an ancestor has transform/filter, which becomes its containing block), sticky (flows, then STICKS within its scroll container and nearest scrolling ancestor's edge — the hybrid). HIDING: display:none removes from RENDER TREE and ACCESSIBILITY tree, layout closes the gap; visibility:hidden paints nothing, layout KEEPS the space, a11y-hidden; opacity:0 paints transparently, KEEPS space, still interactive + accessible — pair with pointer-events:none or visibility for the disabled state. The pairs decide: is the element IN FLOW (relative), ANCHORED (absolute/fixed), or PHASED (sticky)?; and should hiding close space (display), keep space (visibility), or keep interactivity (opacity)?

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
Both decision tables, verified:

```css
/* POSITION — the five behaviors */
.static   { position: static; }    /* flow; top/left ignored */
.relative { position: relative; top: -4px; }  /* STILL IN FLOW — offsets
                                                  VISUALLY; original gap kept */
.absolute { position: absolute; inset: 0; }   /* OUT OF FLOW — anchored to
                                                  nearest POSITIONED ancestor;
                                                  siblings close the gap */
.fixed    { position: fixed; top: 0; }          /* OUT OF FLOW — anchored to
                                                  VIEWPORT (transform-trap!) */
.sticky   { position: sticky; top: 0; }        /* flows UNTIL scrolled to,
                                                  then sticks INSIDE its parent */

/* The absolute setup ritual: */
.card { position: relative; }          /* the anchor */
.card .badge { position: absolute; top: 8px; right: 8px; }  /* overlays */

/* HIDING — the three behaviors */
.gone    { display: none; }        /* removed — space closes, a11y-hidden */
.ghost   { visibility: hidden; }   /* space KEPT — invisible, a11y-hidden */
.faded   { opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; }  /* space kept, still painted,
                                  TRANSPARENT — invisible but interactive if
                                  pointer-events not blocked! */
```

The fixed/transform trap (the one that breaks modals): a parent with transform, filter, perspective, will-change, or backdrop-filter becomes the CONTAINING BLOCK for fixed descendants — the 'fixed modal scrolls with the page' bug is an animated/transformed ancestor. Diagnose by walking ancestors for those properties. The sticky constraints (its two gotchas): the PARENT must have room to stick within (a sticky header inside a short parent unsticks fast) and the scroll CONTAINER is the nearest scrollable ancestor — overflow: hidden/scroll on a mid-ancestor changes what it sticks against; also a sticky element loses its stick without a top/bottom offset set.

The hiding choice (what each is FOR): display:none — true removal (conditional UI; but it REMOVES from a11y too — screen readers won't announce it, which is right for hidden chrome, wrong for skip-links); visibility:hidden — layout-stable state changes (keep the layout, hide the content — the animated reveal works because visibility is animatable discretely); opacity:0 — visual-only states (transitions! opacity ANIMATES smoothly — the fade pattern — pair with pointer-events:none or the invisible element swallows clicks).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P{positioning goal} -->|in flow, shift a bit| REL[relative — gap kept]
    P -->|anchor to ancestor| ABS[absolute — set a positioned parent FIRST]
    P -->|viewport anchored| FIX[fixed — check for transformed ancestors]
    P -->|scroll-pinned within parent| STK[sticky — needs top offset + roomy parent]
    H{hiding goal} -->|remove + close space + a11y| DN[display none]
    H -->|keep space, hide visually| VH[visibility hidden]
    H -->|animate, keep interaction control| OP[opacity 0 + pointer-events none]
    TRAP[transform filter will-change on ancestor] --> CB[becomes containing block — fixed breaks]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The containing-block rules (the full map — memorize the triggers): for absolute — nearest ancestor with position non-static, transform, filter, will-change, contain; for fixed — normally the viewport, but ANY ancestor with transform/filter/perspective/will-change/backdrop-filter/contain creates a new containing block; for sticky — the nearest scrollport (scroll container) plus the parent for the stick RANGE. The modal/dropdown bug class ('works on the demo page, breaks in our animated app shell') is almost always this list.

The render-tree consequence (why the hiding trio differs at the ENGINE level): display:none means the element never enters the RENDER tree — no geometry, no a11y, children all hidden (and unhideable individually); visibility:hidden keeps GEOMETRY (the box exists, paint skipped) and inherits to children — but a child can set visibility: visible and REAPPEAR (the classic difference-prover); opacity:0 keeps geometry AND paint (fully rendered, alpha 0 — hence animatable and interactive) — and it creates a STACKING CONTEXT (the surprise z-index consequence when fading elements start covering things).

The composites (the modern patterns the trio builds): 'visually hidden but screen-reader available' — the .sr-only clip pattern (1px box, clip-path, NOT display:none — the accessible-label technique); 'temporarily hidden with animation' — visibility + opacity + transition in a group (visibility toggles at the boundary so the fade isn't interactive at 0); 'disabled' — the inert attribute (the platform's REAL answer: aria-hidden + pointer-events + focus removal in one attribute — the modern replacement for the opacity/pointer-events hand-rolled version). Name inert and the answer reads current.
